name: Fresnedillas de la Oliva bunkers
story: Nationalist troops took Fresnedillas de la Oliva on 5 November 1936 during the advance on Madrid; the front then halted on the Perales river and saw heavy fighting in December 1936. In 1937 the Nationalists fortified the heights around the village with machine-gun nests, trenches and catenary-vaulted shelters, forming part of the western front of Madrid. Several of these positions, including those of Cota 960, can be visited along local paths.
see: Concrete machine-gun posts, connecting trenches and vaulted storage shelters around the village.
plan: One bunker is by the M-521 towards Robledo de Chavela; others require short walks. Free.
